The system information payload starts with signed seconds since boot, then three unsigned load averages for one five and fifteen minutes, then total and free main memory plus shared and buffered memory, then total and free swap, then a 16-bit live process count with explicit padding for m68k, then total and free high memory, then a 32-bit byte unit for all memory fields, then spare trailing bytes sized as twenty minus twice unsigned long size minus 32-bit size to preserve historic sizing.
Load average scaling uses SI_LOAD_SHIFT as 16, so reported load integers are fixed point with that binary point.

The per-task record is versioned and grows by appending. It opens with a 16-bit version and 32-bit exit status, an 8-bit accounting flag set and 8-bit nice value, then CPU wait count and total, block IO wait count and total, swap-in wait count and total, plus cumulative wall-clock and virtual CPU run totals in nanoseconds that wrap silently while counts keep advancing.

After delays the record carries command storage sized by a shared length constant, scheduling discipline with alignment padding, user and group and process and parent identifiers, a 32-bit start time plus 64-bit elapsed and user and system times in microseconds, minor and major fault counts, accumulated resident and virtual memory products, high watermarks for resident and virtual size, byte and syscall counts for read and write, then storage byte counts for read and write and cancelled write.

Later extensions add voluntary and involuntary switch counts, scaled user and system times plus scaled run total, paired count and total for free-pages wait and thrashing wait, a 64-bit start time, compact wait, thread group identity with group elapsed time and executable device and inode, write-copy wait, interrupt wait, per-category delay minima and maxima, and per-category timestamps recording when each maximum occurred.

TASKSTATS_VERSION is 17 and TS_COMM_LEN is 32 with a requirement that it cover the scheduler command length, and presence of TASKSTATS_HAS_IO_ACCOUNTING signals that per-task storage accounting fields exist.
Both user headers use once-only inclusion guards with _LINUX_SYSINFO_H and _LINUX_TASKSTATS_H preventing repeated inclusion.

Numeric sysctl identifiers form stable compatibility ABI with intentional gaps and retained obsolete slots, negative minus two and minus three reserved for aggregate selectors, and distant values plus unnumbered sentinels marking extension points rather than dense sequences.

Task statistics versions only grow by appending while keeping earlier offsets, delay totals wrap to zero on overflow while counts still advance, some eight-byte members carry explicit eight-byte alignment, and a newer 64-bit start time coexists with legacy 32-bit start time.
Block IO count and total plus swap-in count and total are updated atomically under the task delay lock, while CPU wait count and total are explicitly documented as not atomically updated.

Consumers must handle 32-bit start-time range limits, silent nanosecond total wraparound, explicit padding and alignment differences across word sizes, sparse and obsolete sysctl numbers that must not be compacted, and truncated command names limited by the shared length.
System information and per-task statistics records plus all enumerated sysctl number groups are stable user to kernel interface payloads and identifiers that user space may rely on.
